decisions.reason: The tracked text edits change the authoritative revision to integrate, but do not change the editorial objective or explicitly supersede either approved rewrite.
The authoritative manuscript revision does not change the publisher attribution; the copyright-page question is a separate clause in the same message.
Tracked manuscript edits do not alter the requested publication-readiness guidance; that guidance is independently established by another clause in the message.
The general tracked text edits do not necessarily change the Chapter 12 hierarchy and capitalization requirements, which are independently addressed in the same message.
The client-edited manuscript text does not change the paperback cover requirements; the cover feedback is a separate clause.
Tracked text edits do not change the aspect-ratio or cropping requirements for chapter images.
The revised manuscript text does not necessarily change the selected images or the criteria for assessing their tone and colour-palette fit.
The authoritative text revision leaves the inclusion, selection, timing, and beginning-of-chapter placement of images unchanged.
Nothing in the tracked-edit statement indicates that the title or the previously removed literal newline artifact changed.
